prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core theme: “Time for Common Sense.” Trust people over government; strengthen families, communities, and national institutions; cut taxes and regulation; restore choice in public services; protect national independence.

Families and education
- Tax cuts for families: boost Children’s Tax Credit for under-5s; restore a Married Couple’s Allowance (transferable allowance for families with children under 11/carers); remove tax on Widowed Parent benefits; reform Working Families Tax Credit to be paid to the caring parent; Family Scholarships for return-to-work training.
- Schools: “Free Schools” with autonomy for heads/governors; cut bureaucracy; easier exclusions with specialist Progress Centres; direct per-pupil funding and allow successful schools to expand; enable new schools by parents/faith/charities; parent-triggered Ofsted and management change.
- Students/universities: raise loan repayment threshold to £20k; no top-up fees; create permanent university endowments to secure autonomy.

Law and order
- More police, less paperwork; “cops in shops” and parish constables; tackle antisocial behavior.
- Expand Secure Training Centres; link release to behavior/qualifications.
- Mandatory jail for dealers selling to under-16s; tougher action near schools.
- Honest sentencing (end automatic early release); prison work to fund reparation/families.
- Lifetime supervision options for sex offenders; protect children online.
- Victims’ rights with named contacts; reform self-defence and double jeopardy.

Economy and tax
- Keep the pound; enhance Bank of England MPC independence; new Council of Economic Advisers and National Accounts Commission.
- £8bn annual tax cuts funded by savings outside schools/NHS/police/defence: abolish tax on most savings/dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000 (1m out of tax); new Married Couple’s Allowance; cut petrol/diesel duty by 6p; business rates cuts; repeal IR35; CGT simplification.
- Deregulation: new Deregulation Commission with regulatory budgets; small business exemptions; focus utility regulators on competition; abolish Climate Change Levy; review nuclear energy.

Health
- Match NHS spending plans but end political micromanagement.
- Patient’s Guarantee: maximum waits by clinical need (start with cancer/cardiac), choice of hospital (NHS or private, NHS-funded).
- Empower Ward Sisters/bring back Matron; expand surgical units; broaden practice nurse roles; Exceptional Medicines Fund; remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable; increase hospice funding to 40%.

Older people
- Higher basic pension (extra for over-75s); option to consolidate winter fuel/TV licence into tax-free pension uplift.
- Abolish compulsory annuity purchase at 75; consult on funded pension option for young workers.
- Free nursing care; protect savers from punitive long-term care costs.

Sovereignty, defence, and asylum
- In Europe, not run by Europe: keep the pound and veto; renegotiate Nice; reserve powers in UK law; complete single market; tackle EU fraud.
- Defence: meet manning, oppose political correctness; exempt forces from ECHR; no EU army outside NATO; support US missile defence; maintain nuclear deterrent; strengthen reserves.
- Aid: work toward 0.7% GNP; more via charities; reform EU aid; push global free trade by 2020.
- Asylum: secure reception centres, safe-country rule, fast removals.

Society and welfare
- Office of Civil Society; abolish irrecoverable VAT for charities (funded from euro-prep budgets).
- Replace New Deal with “Britain Works” (payment by results and job retention); Can Work, Must Work; lone parents with children 11+ to seek work; improve disabled savings rules; Incapacity Benefit agency with rehab; national anti-fraud squad; clean NI numbers.

Town, country, transport, environment
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP; honest food labelling; animal welfare.
- Support rural services (rate cuts, fuel rebates for community transport, benefit card to protect post offices); scrap housebuilding targets; protect “Blue Belts”; rural select committee.
- Urban regeneration companies; extra policing; partner schools; brownfield first; tackle antisocial tenants; expand home ownership (RTB, rent-to-mortgage, homesteading).
- Transport: 6p fuel duty cut; invest in roads/public transport; Roads Standards Unit; consider 80mph where safe; charge foreign lorries (Brit Disc); revive rail; support London Underground reforms.
- Environment: emissions trading, energy efficiency, renewables, cleaner generation.

Culture, media, democracy
- £3bn endowment for arts from Channel 4 sale and Lottery surplus; boost tourism; protect school sport and playing fields; charitable status for sports clubs.
- Single media/communications regulator; privatise Channel 4 (retain PSB remit); modernise ownership rules; fair BBC oversight; access for religious broadcasters.
- Strengthen local councils (free councils); local referendums for big council tax rises; scrap regional bodies; English votes for English laws; strengthen Lords (independent, elected element); tougher parliamentary scrutiny; keep FPTP; uphold Belfast Agreement and security.
- Fewer ministers, MPs (after reforms), and special advisers.
